title: Can I BEAT Drawback Chess?
summary: First Drawback Chess video (highly requested): each player is randomly assigned a hidden drawback. Goal: win three games. His drawbacks include Stage Fright (can't move to the four centre squares - so no London, he plays b3 double fianchetto) and Bongcloud (when your king is on the back rank you can only move pawns and kings). Opponents' revealed drawbacks: Secret Garden (a secret area in front of your pawns...), can't take knights, Diplomatic Immunity (can't capture a piece that just moved unless that move was a capture), Femme Fatale (can only capture the enemy king with a queen). He reaches three wins.
rules: Standard start; random secret drawback for each side, revealed after the game.
Win by capturing the enemy king (drawback site rules) or by the opponent breaking a losing drawback.

Drawbacks seen: Lame Duck - can't move your king; Pac-Man - if you can take a pawn you must; True Gentleman - can never capture the queen; Stage Fright - can't move to the center four squares (d4,e4,d5,e5 tinted pink); Bongcloud - when your king is on the back rank you can only move pawns and kings; Secret Garden - hidden squares in front of your pawns (if the opponent moves there you lose; inferred from rules entry); Diplomatic Immunity - you can't capture a piece that just moved unless that move was a capture; Femme Fatale - you can only capture the enemy king with a queen; a 'can't capture knights' drawback.
win_condition: Capture the enemy king or opponent drawback loss. Series goal: 3 wins.

opponent.name: Online humans on the drawback site (e.g. Earth_Based_Human)

board.theme_notes: Brown/cream board on purple background; forbidden squares tinted pink for Stage Fright.

events: Post-game reveal of both drawbacks with difficulty comparison.
